695d2bdf9c103cd607cdab89cffb8d32bd111f3c.summary: A research paper (IEEE S&P 2017, co-authored by researchers from the University of California, Santa Barbara and Georgia Institute of Technology) describes Android attacks that combine the 'draw on top' and accessibility permissions to take control of the UI feedback loop. The attacks covered include clickjacking, keystroke recording, stealthy phishing, silent installation of an app with all permissions, and phone unlocking while the screen is off. The report says the attacks were still practical on Android 7.1.2 with June 2017 patches. It describes a responsible disclosure timeline from…

hedges: Most of these attacks are due to design issues, so they are challenging to prevent.
The authors say some of this functionality works as intended, but that it can still be abused.
Previous Android versions are very likely to be vulnerable as well.
Google's rationale for automatically granting draw-on-top is only stated to the best of the authors' understanding.
The authors believe the attacks are practical, based on a user study with 20 subjects.
Google's partial fix applies only on Android 7.1.2 and only to normal permissions, not special ones.
Some reported bugs were marked won't fix and so will not be fixed.
The proof-of-concept is withheld because the attacks can still be launched against real users.

69c39d827a80d7a560dbafc31cce36566ec37c7f.summary: Symantec white paper on the 2022 ransomware outlook. It says targeted ransomware attacks rose through 2021 and profiles active groups and families, including Birdwing (Pysa), Sirex (AvosLocker), Pinion (Hive), Dryxiphia (Yanluowang), Batfly (Nemty, Karma), Pollen (Zeppelin), Miner (Conti), Coreid (Darkside, BlackMatter) and Hispid (Grief, Macaw). It covers pre-ransomware tools, exploited VPN and Exchange flaws, the Noberus Rust-coded strain, the Exmatter exfiltration tool, the SquirrelWaffle loader, Emotet's return, and the REvil takedown and arrests.

hedges: It is not entirely clear if Birdwing deploys the ransomware itself, or if it operates a ransomware-as-a-service (RaaS) model.
The report says Pysa may stand for a phrase found in Birdwing ransom notes.
It is not clear if the Emotet return was driven by Miner itself or by an affiliate user of Conti.
It is unclear whether Yanluowang is rented out to affiliates or whether Dryxiphia carries out most attacks directly.
Confirmed attacks from known targeted ransomware families are probably only a representative sample of the overall number of attacks.
The Symantec statistics should be treated as a representative sample of attacks blocked by Symantec products.
Exmatter is likely the product of a ransomware affiliate rather than Coreid or Miner.
The report says BlackMatter's shutdown likely means arrests made continuing to run the ransomware difficult.
